themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% increase (z-score 14.74)—suggesting a new or recently intensified activity or event is disrupting CD 405 parks.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,900% spike)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No Reddit or local news mentions suggest this may be very recent or unreported
reporting_angles: What new activity or event triggered the spike? (concert, sports league, construction, weekend gatherings)
Interview residents near affected parks about timing, frequency, and impact on quality of life

themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 6 this week from a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 586% increase (z-score 4.87)—indicating either new vendor activity or a sudden shift in enforcement patterns in Ridgewood/Glendale.
evidence: 6 vendor enforcement complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% spike)
Z-score of 4.87 signals statistically significant change
No prior local news coverage suggests emerging rather than established issue
reporting_angles: Has DOE or City enforcement ramped up operations in CD 405 this week?
Are street vendors expanding in previously unregulated areas (Fresh Pond Road, Cypress Avenue near rezonings)?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 300% increase (z-score 5.2)—coupled with food establishment complaints at 8 (205% spike, z-score 4.41), suggesting potential health code violations or contamination incidents at local establishments.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 5.2)
8 food establishment complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (205% spike, z-score 4.41)
Convergence of two food-safety metrics suggests systemic rather than isolated issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOH inspection records—which establishments are flagged?
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timing, and which restaurants/vendors they visited

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Use Violations
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints spiked to 24 last week from a baseline of 10.1 per week—a 137% increase (z-score 5.4)—with 426 DOB permits filed over 90 days (330 alterations), suggesting either widespread unpermitted work or increased code enforcement activity tied to development activity.
evidence: 24 building/use complaints last week vs. 10.1 weekly average (137% spike, z-score 5.4)
426 DOB filings in past 90 days, 330 alterations—high construction activity baseline
Three active ULURP rezonings (Fresh Pond Road, Cypress Avenue, 57th Drive) may be triggering renovation waves
reporting_angles: Are unpermitted alterations occurring near rezoning sites as property owners speculate on zoning changes?
Is DOB conducting heightened inspection sweeps in preparation for planned rezonings?

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints (Earlier Alert)
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints reached 11 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.8 per week—a 300% increase (z-score 5.58)—though no follow-up spike this week; may indicate resolved incident or data lag worth clarifying.
evidence: 11 safety complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 5.58)
No safety complaints visible in current week data—unclear if resolved or delayed reporting
No community board agendas or Reddit discussions to provide context on nature of safety incidents
reporting_angles: What triggered the 3-week-old safety spike? Was it a specific incident or sustained pattern?
Check with NYPD and CB 305 for context on what residents were reporting
